title: Nuclear Fusion Energy
text: Nuclear fusion is the process by which two light atomic nuclei (typically hydrogen isotopes deuterium and tritium) combine to form a heavier nucleus (helium), releasing enormous amounts of energy. It is the process that powers the Sun. Unlike nuclear fission, fusion produces no long-lived radioactive waste and its fuel (hydrogen isotopes) is abundant. Achieving controlled fusion on Earth has been a goal of researchers since the 1950s. The main experimental approaches are magnetic confinement fusion (tokamaks, like ITER being built in France) and inertial confinement fusion (using lasers, like NIF in California). In December 2022, NIF achieved ignition — fusion producing more energy than the lasers delivered.
